text:
No questions needed. Switching channels isn't in the ask-first list, and this doesn't touch any repo, token, or file of yours. Setup keeps your existing settings and only changes the channel.

Check the current state first:

```sh
tentmaker version --json
tentmaker status --json
```

Save the dev channel (this keeps every other value and restarts the service, but running jobs keep going), then install the dev build:

```sh
sudo tentmaker setup --yes --json --channel dev
sudo tentmaker update --json
```

I'd run `update` as a second command rather than `update --channel dev` alone. The standalone form installs one dev build but leaves auto-updates on the saved stable channel.

Then verify:

```sh
tentmaker version --json
tentmaker doctor --json
```

Success means setup exits 0 with every entry in its `steps` succeeded, `version` shows a dev build (like `0.1.1-dev.<timestamp>.<sha>`), and `doctor` exits 0. If `doctor` reports a problem, I'll apply its `fix` and rerun it. If an update leaves the service unhealthy, it rolls back on its own after 60 seconds. You can also run `sudo tentmaker rollback`.
